title: Professional advisers: when to ask, and what to bring
audience: Owners in any service business who are deciding how to structure, register, brand, insure or premise the business.
learningOutcomes: Name the adviser needed for each business decision, and the decision it supports
Prepare a one-page brief with the facts an adviser needs before a meeting
Confirm ownership of business assets, and record each piece of advice, the decision and who made it

instruction.heading: Advice is a cost you choose to spend
instruction.body: Some decisions in a service business need a specialist. The skill is to match the adviser to the decision, bring a short brief, and record what you were told. Advice is worth paying for when a decision is hard to reverse, when a large amount of money is at stake, or when a mistake would be costly to fix. Where you can, ask for a fixed-fee quote, and say which question you need answered.

instruction.heading: Business structure
instruction.body: The main structures are a sole trader, a partnership, a company and a franchise. Each one shapes who is liable for the business's debts and how much paperwork it takes. A lawyer should advise on the structure you choose, and an accountant should advise on the tax and cash consequences. The source describes the same set of structures, and treats a lawyer as essential for the founding documents of a company or partnership.

instruction.heading: Money, records and tax
instruction.body: An accountant can help set up the records that show money coming in and going out. Ask for a simple system that records each invoice, expense and payment in one place, with a reference number on each. Keep the advice in writing.

instruction.heading: Brand, website and design
instruction.body: A web developer or graphic designer can help shape the visual identity and a website that explains the service clearly. Before you pay, check who will own the domain name, the logins, the design files and the content. The business should hold these in its own name, so that it keeps control if the designer changes. Confirm the arrangement in writing.

instruction.heading: Insurance, premises and contracts
instruction.body: An insurance broker can compare policies and build cover around the risks of the work. Compare quotes on the same scope, limits, exclusions and conditions. A real estate agent can help find premises, and a lawyer should review a lease before you sign it. Contractors can carry out repair and maintenance of the premises you use.

instruction.heading: Prepare a brief and record the advice
instruction.body: Before a meeting, write a one-page brief. Include the business and the decision, the facts an adviser needs, the numbers you already hold, the deadline, and the question you want answered. After the meeting, record the advice, the decision you made, who made it and when. This record protects the business if the decision is questioned later.

procedure: Write the decision, the facts and the deadline in a one-page brief
Choose the adviser that matches the decision
Ask for a fixed-fee quote or a written scope of work
Take the advice, and note any step it leaves open
Check that business assets, such as the domain name and design files, are held in the business's name
Record the advice, the decision, the person who made it and the date

workedExamples.situation: Tom is a trainer who plans to form a company and rent a small studio. He is not sure whether to see a lawyer, an accountant or an insurance broker first.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What should Tom ask for, and in what order?
workedExamples.reasoning: He should take advice on the structure first, because the structure affects liability and paperwork. An accountant should then look at cash flow and the tax consequences. An insurance broker should compare cover for the studio and the work on the same scope. A lawyer should review the lease before he signs. He prepares a brief for each adviser and records the advice.

workedExamples.situation: Sara runs a small cleaning business and has a designer build her website. The designer keeps the domain and the design files in his own account.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What should Sara do before final payment?
workedExamples.reasoning: She should ask the designer to transfer the domain, the logins and the design files into the business's name, and confirm this in writing before final payment. If the business holds these assets, a change of designer will not cut off the website or the brand.

equipmentAndPpe: No PPE is needed for this lesson
A record of advice and decisions
An asset register for the domain name, logins and design files

commonErrors.error: Going to an adviser without a brief, so the advice is general
commonErrors.prevention: Write a one-page brief before each meeting.

commonErrors.error: Assuming the designer or developer holds the business's assets
commonErrors.prevention: Confirm ownership of the domain, logins and files in writing.

commonErrors.error: Comparing insurance quotes on price alone
commonErrors.prevention: Compare on the same scope, limits, exclusions and conditions.

commonErrors.error: Signing a lease without legal review
commonErrors.prevention: Have a lawyer review the lease before signing, and record the advice.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: See also the insurance lesson “Insurance for property trade work in Australia”.
A recommendation to seek legal review is not a legal conclusion.

qualityStandard: Each adviser decision has a one-page brief dated before the meeting
Advice is recorded in writing, with the decision, the person and the date
Ownership of the domain name, logins and design files is confirmed in the business's name
Insurance quotes are compared on the same scope, limits, exclusions and conditions
documentationEvidence: Written advice and decision record for each adviser
Asset register showing who holds the domain name, logins and design files
Insurance comparison sheet on the same scope
summary: Match the adviser to the decision: structure, money, brand, insurance and premises
Bring a one-page brief, and get advice in writing
Check who owns the business's domain name, logins and files
Compare insurance on the same terms, and record every decision

knowledgeChecks.question: Which adviser should advise on the legal structure of the business?
Before a meeting with an adviser, what should you prepare?
options: A list of competitor prices only and no decision or deadline at all
A one-page brief with the decision, the facts, the deadline and the question
Nothing, because the adviser will ask every question and you need not prepare at all

knowledgeChecks.question: Why check who holds the domain name and the design files for your brand?
options: So the website ranks higher in search results and the name is easy to find
Because the law requires the designer to hold them in every case
So the business keeps control of its own assets if the designer changes
